target_customer: Real estate developers in Latin America selling new properties, and their home buyers needing mortgages
problem: Selling new homes and closing mortgages involves many intermediaries and slow paperwork; Vecindario claims its online flow is 6x faster.
business_model: Commission or software fees from developers on property sales and mortgage placement, plus Vecindario Suite sales software (fee structure not sourced)
product_category: Proptech sales and mortgage platform for new housing

founders.name: Felipe Restrepo
previous_startups: Habla Creativo, digital real estate agency
founders.background_notes: YC page: over ten years in tech focused on real estate and banking, advised Colombian construction firms.

founders.name: Camilo Ruiz
education: Master's in UX and UI (institution not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: graphic designer with about ten years as an entrepreneur.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as Inactive, yet Forbes Colombia reported growth in June 2023 and no closure was found.

competitors.name: La Haus
competitors.what: Medellin based proptech selling homes online across LatAm
competitors.traction_then: Valuation above $100M reported after its Series B
competitors.funding_then: $35M Series B led by Greenspring, per Forbes Colombia

competitors.name: Habi
competitors.what: Colombian proptech that buys existing homes, adjacent to Vecindario's new home sales
competitors.traction_then: Described as the largest homebuyer in Colombia

technical_complexity.rationale: A sales and mortgage workflow platform is standard web engineering; the hard parts are bank integrations and operations rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Developer relationships and listings of more than 20,000 apartments in 18 cities by November 2021 (La Republica) help, but portals and proptechs could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A 2022 ecosystem article groups these firms with Vecindario as corporate proptech players; no source shows any of them copying or buying Vecindario.

market_need_then: Colombia has a housing deficit and La Nota Economica reports that 7 in 10 Colombians feel they cannot own a home; developers also needed faster sales and mortgage approval.

branding.domain_note: Uses vecindario.com (exact .com). The site could not be fetched from this environment.

brand_strength.rationale: Spanish word for neighborhood fits the home buying theme and the company got Forbes and La Republica coverage, but no source speaks about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Selling new homes and mortgages directly
pivots.to: Also selling Vecindario Suite, software for real estate projects
pivots.why: Forbes Colombia says it recently launched Vecindario Suite to make any project's sales process more efficient; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Vecindario grew to about 87 people and reported more than 1 billion pesos in processed transactions by mid 2023, which makes it an unusually large company for a record marked Inactive. No closure, layoffs or bankruptcy were found, so the Inactive flag is unexplained and the cause of any decline is not public. Funding amounts are undisclosed in every source found.
notes: Descubre says 2 rounds with the latest on 2022-07-15 and no amounts; this rests on one database. A Caplight page shows a $16M Series A headline for a company named Caplight, which is not a Vecindario round. The Habi and La Haus competitor entries are adjacent rivals in Colombian proptech, with sources dated before the batch.
